newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 26.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on the front page on November 26:

WASHINGTON - Pacific Rim nations vowed to eliminate nearly all tariffs on computers, semiconductors, faxes, software and telephone equipment in the next three years, bowing to a last-minute personal appeal from President Clinton.
WASHINGTON - David Kessler, who extended the regulatory authority of the Food and Drug Administration over products from orange juice to tobacco announced that he will resign early next year.
SANTA MONICA - O.J. Simpson testified that he had no explanation for the cuts on his hand and the blood found in his car and his estate after the murder of his ex-wife and her friend.
WASHINGTON - Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle signaled independence from the Clinton Administration on issues ranging from Social Security, Medicare, and welfare to campaign finance reform.

SVETLOGORSK, Belarus - A wave of HIV, nearly all of it borne by 20-something addicts using dirty needles had blown through this town with the fury of a medieval plague and is spreading fast in Russia, Ukraine and Belarus.
TOKYO - An American held captive on spy charges for three months in North Korea will be released, according to the U.S. Embassy.
